items.claim: The rationale's colon-position description of the shared 'abomination to YHWH' construct phrase is byte-false: the phrase does not 'open the second colon' in either verse, so the stated warrant misdescribes the actual hook-word structure even though the underlying cluster call survives.
items.evidence: Accent-based re-derivation from oshb bytes: in oshb:Prov.15.8, the atnach (the verse-medial disjunctive accent) falls on יְהוָ֑ה itself, so זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה is the ENTIRE first colon and תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה is that colon's own closing two words — not the opening of a second colon (colon 2 is וּתְפִלַּ֖ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים רְצוֹנֽוֹ, which does not contain the shared phrase at all). In oshb:Prov.15.9, the atnach falls on רָשָׁ֑ע, so תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע is itself the first colon, and the shared phrase opens THAT colon — i.e. it opens colon 1 / the verse, again not 'colon 2'. Across the pair the phrase is therefore colon-1-final in 15:8 and colon-1/verse-initial in 15:9 (a hook-word link straddling the verse boundary), not the uniform 'both open colon 2' pattern the rationale states. This does not overturn the cluster call itself: sweep.py --skel 'תועבת יהוה' (byte tier, object named: the exact 2-word construct phrase) returns 11 verses book-wide (Prov.3.32, 11.1, 11.20, 12.22, 15.8, 15.9, 15.26, 16.5, 17.15, 20.10, 20.23), and 15.8-15.9 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them, so the row's own 'sweep: 2 consecutive verses' digit is independently confirmed correct and the catchword-adjacency ground for the proverb_cluster survives. Both inline Hebrew quotes collate at byte tier via collate.py against oshb:Prov.15.8 and oshb:Prov.15.9 respectively, so this is a structural-description defect in the stated warrant, not a quotation-fidelity or citation defect.
